You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Ford Motor Company China assembly joint venture, realized record ~2015-2016 (3-4 years after closing)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier contains ONLY the realized
> post-closing record within the fixed 3-5-year outcome window; it contains no
> information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status (feasibility-relevant)
- Ford Motor Company continued filing annual reports on Form 10-K throughout the
  outcome window; the joint venture is reported as an unconsolidated equity-method
  affiliate within Ford's own consolidated 10-K rather than as a separately
  SEC-registered entity. [SRC: SEC accession 0000037996-17-000013, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- The outcome window is fixed to Ford's Form 10-K for fiscal year 2016 (filed
  2017-02-09), which reports full-year 2016 results together with year-over-year
  comparisons to 2015 and 2014 — approximately 3 to 4 years after the November 30,
  2012 restructuring. [SRC: SEC accession 0000037996-17-000013, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Realized scale of the venture
- By year-end 2016, Changan Ford Automobile Corporation, Ltd. ("CAF") "currently
  operates five assembly plants, an engine plant, and a transmission plant in China,"
  up from the single retained Chongqing facility (plus two assembly plants, an engine
  plant, and a transmission plant reported as under construction at the time of the
  2012 restructuring). [SRC: SEC accession 0000037996-17-000013, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- Ford's carrying value of its equity investment in CAF (50% ownership) was $1,307
  million at year-end 2015 and $1,315 million at year-end 2016. [SRC: SEC accession 0000037996-17-000013, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- The related three-way Changan Ford Mazda Engine Company, Ltd. ("CFME") joint venture
  (Ford 25%, Mazda 25%, Changan 50%) continued unchanged, with Ford's investment
  carrying value of $77 million (2015) and $80 million (2016). [SRC: SEC accession 0000037996-17-000013, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Realized earnings contribution and trend
- Ford's China joint ventures (including CAF) contributed $1.5 billion to the Asia
  Pacific segment's pre-tax profit in 2015, described as "$234 million higher than"
  2014. [SRC: SEC accession 0000037996-17-000013, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- Those same China joint ventures contributed $1.4 billion to Asia Pacific's pre-tax
  profit in 2016, "$75 million lower than in 2015"; their net income margin was 14.6%
  in 2016, "a reduction of 1 percentage point from 2015," which the filing attributes
  to "negative industry pricing in China and a higher mix of vehicles with engine
  displacement of 1.6 liters or lower." [SRC: SEC accession 0000037996-17-000013, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- At the Asia Pacific segment level, full-year pre-tax profit was a record $765 million
  in 2015 (up 29% from 2014), then $627 million in 2016 (down $138 million from 2015),
  which the filing attributes to "lower net pricing, adverse exchange effects (mainly a
  weaker Chinese renminbi), and unfavorable cost performance." [SRC: SEC accession 0000037996-17-000013, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Items not found in the retrieved filing
- The retrieved FY2016 Form 10-K contains no reference to Changan Mazda Automobile
  Corporation ("CMA"), the Mazda/Changan entity formed in the 2012 split, and no
  statement on whether the 2012 contract-manufacturing bridge between CMA and CAF was
  completed, extended, or disrupted after its stated 2014 end date. [UNVERIFIED: post-2014 status of the CMA/CAF contract-manufacturing bridge]
- No dispute, renegotiation, divestiture, or dissolution involving CAF, Changan, or
  Ford's China operations is disclosed in the retrieved filing. [UNVERIFIED: any unresolved dispute or renegotiation affecting CAF]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Within the fixed 3-4-year outcome window, the joint venture's disclosed record shows
  physical and financial growth (one retained plant to five assembly plants plus
  engine and transmission plants; investment carrying value up from $1,307 million to
  $1,315 million) alongside a documented one-percentage-point margin decline (to 14.6%)
  and a $75 million year-over-year drop in pre-tax profit contribution in 2016,
  attributed by the filing to negative China industry pricing; the wider Asia Pacific
  segment's pre-tax profit likewise declined from a record $765 million (2015) to $627
  million (2016). [SRC: SEC accession 0000037996-17-000013, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

[SLICE END]
